subject: Cross-track title placement decision for Greenleaf candidate (E. Brooks)
messages:
From: Candice Holmes <candice@talentpros.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenleaf Recruiting <recruiting@greenleaf.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Candidate offer — quick level check for Ethan Brooks

Hi Priyom,

Quick context: Greenleaf just completed onsite interviews for Ethan Brooks (ML infra lead background, 6 yrs at mid-stage infra startup, small people manager for 3). Hiring manager is leaning toward L5 manager track but recruiting flagged cross-track placement could be L5 senior IC instead. Before we finalize the offer packet, can you confirm whether Redwood should route this as an L5 Manager or L5 Senior IC for comp-banding and title?

Key notes attached: a short resume summary and the hiring manager's scoring. CompBench sent a mid-market range that overlaps L5/L6 bands.

High-level ask: any objection to placing as L5 Senior IC (individual contributor) with potential manager path in 6–12 months? If Manager track is insisted on, they need a stronger justification for an immediate manager title (scope, direct reports >3, org impact).

Thanks — Candice

Attachments: Greenleaf_EB_resume.pdf (resume stub), comp-benchmarks_L4-L6.xlsx (benchmark stub)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate offer — quick level check for Ethan Brooks

Team — forwarding Candice's note. Quick read: Ethan has strong infra/latency expertise and has led a small team; hiring manager stresses people-first hire for the new inference infra squad. Recruiting is worried about stretching the manager band without direct, sustained people management experience.

My thoughts:
- Scope: He would own a new infra area (service-level design + runtime optimizations) and be IC-influential across two teams. That leans toward a Senior IC (L5) by scope but not obviously manager-level (no >3 direct reports).
- Compensation: CompBench median for L5 Manager sits ~10–12% above the L5 IC median. If we mark manager, we'd need to justify that uplift vs. bench/commensurate scope.
- Risk: Offering Manager title now creates expectations for direct org decisions; if promotion is likely in 6 months, we could include a documented development plan and a fast-track promotion clause.

Options to approve today (pick one):
1) Offer L5 Senior IC + competitive band (salary + RSU target midway to manager band) + 6-month review clause for manager conversion.
2) Offer L5 Manager with higher comp (requires sign-off from Laura for band exception and an HC note).

I've attached the comp benchmarks. Please reply with preferred option and any required approvals.

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachment: comp-benchmarks_L4-L6.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate offer — quick level check for Ethan Brooks

+1 for Option 1 (L5 Senior IC + fast-track). A few operational notes:
- HC: this hire is already in HC request HC-297 approved for a senior infra engineer (IC). If we convert to Manager track, we need an HC reclass via People Ops.
- SLA: manager band will push base target higher and impacts forecasted budget for Q2. We should avoid band exceptions unless clear org-level need.
- Candidate expectations: be explicit in offer letter that promotion timeline is objective-based (6 months), include clear success criteria.

If Laura signs off on the fast-track clause and comp midpoint uplift (5–8% RSU/top-off), I can proceed to finalize the offer template and cc recruiting.

—Karthik

Approved: Option 1 with clarifying language.

Decision summary for the record:
- Title/Level: L5 Senior Individual Contributor
- Compensation: base within L5 band; RSU target set at 7% uplift toward manager median (documented in offer packet).
- Promotion path: 6-month fast-track review with explicit success criteria (service ownership, tri-team collaboration, documented impact metrics).
- HC: maintain HC-297 as IC headcount; no reclass required.

Priyom — please draft the offer letter using the template linked and include the fast-track clause. Karthik, include the comp uplift in the final offer and then loop Candice + Greenleaf recruiting. I'll sign-off the final packet when I see the offer PDF.

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
